sandbox: macOS sandbox-exec: no network, home folder unreadable, one scratch folder writable

tools.name: parse_version
tools.description: Parse a version string into a Version object for comparison operations. version_string: A version string to parse, e.g. '1.0a5' -> '<Version('1.0a5')>'.

tools.name: parse_specifier_set
tools.description: Parse a version specifier string into a SpecifierSet for checking version compatibility. specifiers: A version specifier string, e.g., '>=3.0,!=3.1', or a comma-separated list of specifiers -> string representation of the SpecifierSet object.

tools.name: specifier_set_contains
tools.description: Check if a version is contained within a SpecifierSet. specifier_set: A string representation of the specifier set (e.g., '>=1.0.0,!=1.0.1'), version: The version string to check for containment in the specifier set, prereleases: Whether or not to match prereleases with this SpecifierSet. If set to None (the default), it will follow the recommendation from PEP 440.

tools.name: is_specifier_set_unsatisfiable
tools.description:
Check whether a specifier set can never be satisfied.
    
    A specifier set is unsatisfiable if no version can satisfy all specifiers simultaneously.
    
    Args:
        specifiers (str): A string representation of version specifiers
        
    Returns:
        bool: True if no version can satisfy all specifiers simultaneously
        
    Example:
        >>> is_specifier_set_unsatisfiable(">=2.0,<1.0")
        True

tools.name: specifier_set_to_range
tools.description: Convert a SpecifierSet to a VersionRange string representation. specifiers: A string representation of version specifiers, e.g. '>=1.0,<2.0' -> '<VersionRange '[1.0, 2.0.dev0)'>.

tools.name: range_contains_version
tools.description:
Check if a specific version is contained within a VersionRange.
    
    Args:
        version_range (str): A version range specifier compatible with packaging.specifiers.SpecifierSet
        version (str): The version string to check for containment in the range
        prereleases (bool | None, optional): Whether to match pre-releases. None (default) uses the range's own policy.
        installed (bool | None, optional): When True, accept a pre-release item even if the range would not otherwise allow it.
        
    Returns:
        bool: True if the version is contained in the range, False otherwise.
        
    Example:
        >>> range_contains_version(">=1.0,<2.0", "1.5")
        True

tools.name: get_empty_version_range
tools.description: Return an empty VersionRange that matches no versions. prereleases: whether prereleases should be considered when matching versions -> the empty VersionRange as a string representation.

tools.name: get_singleton_version_range
tools.description: Create a VersionRange that contains only a single specific version. version: A PEP 440 compliant version string, e.g. '1.0' -> VersionRange singleton for 1.0. prereleases: Whether to include pre-release versions; if None, uses the default behavior. Example: get_singleton_version_range('1.0') -> '{1.0}'.

tools.name: is_version_range_subset
tools.description:
Check if one VersionRange is a subset of another. self_range: A version range specifier string for the range to check if it's a subset, other_range: A version range specifier string for the range to check against.
    
    >>> is_version_range_subset('>=1.5,<1.8', '>=1.0,<2.0')
    True

tools.name: intersect_version_ranges
tools.description: Compute the intersection of two version range specifiers. range1: first version range specifier, range2: second version range specifier. e.g. intersect_version_ranges('>=1.0', '<2.0') -> '>=1.0,<2.0'.

tools.name: difference_version_ranges
tools.description:
Compute the difference between two VersionRanges, returning versions in the first but not the second.
    
    Args:
        version_range_a (string): The first version range, expressed as a specifier set string
        version_range_b (string): The second version range to subtract from the first, expressed as a specifier set string
    
    Returns:
        string: The resulting version range as a specifier set string
    
    Example:
        >>> difference_version_ranges(">=1.0", ">=2.0")
        '>=1.0,<2.0'

tools.name: filter_versions_by_range
tools.description:
Yield items from iterable whose version falls inside the given version range.
    
    Args:
        version_range_spec: A version range specifier compatible with packaging.specifiers.SpecifierSet
        iterable: An iterable of version strings
        prereleases: Whether to include pre-release versions; None uses PEP 440 default behavior
        
    Returns:
        List of version strings that fall within the specified range
        
    Example:
        >>> filter_versions_by_range(">=1.0,<2.0", ["0.9", "1.5", "2.0"])
        ['1.5']

tools.name: parse_version_string
tools.description:
Parse the given version string.
    
    This is identical to the Version constructor.
    
    >>> parse_version_string('1.0.dev1')
    '1.0.dev1'
    
    :param version: The version string to parse.
    :raises ValueError: When the version string is not a valid version.

tools.name: canonicalize_version_string
tools.description: Return a canonical form of a version string. version: A version string to canonicalize, e.g. '1.0.0' -> '1'. strip_trailing_zero: Whether to strip trailing zeros from the release segment, e.g. '1.0.0' with strip_trailing_zero=False -> '1.0.0'.

tools.name: canonicalize_package_name
tools.description: Normalize a Python package name to its canonical form. name: The name to normalize. validate: Check whether the name is a valid distribution name. >>> canonicalize_package_name('Django') 'django'

tools.name: is_version_prerelease
tools.description: Check if a version is a pre-release version. version: A version string to check if it is a pre-release version -> true if pre-release, false otherwise.

tools.name: get_version_release
tools.description: Get the release components of a version as a tuple. version: A version string to parse, e.g. '1.2.3' -> (1, 2, 3).

tools.name: get_version_pre_release
tools.description: Get the pre-release segment of a version. version: A version string to parse and extract the pre-release segment from -> The pre-release segment as a tuple of (letter, number) or None if no pre-release segment exists.

tools.name: get_version_post_release
tools.description:
Get the post-release number of a version. version: A version string to parse and extract the post-release number from
    
    >>> print(get_version_post_release("1.2.3"))
    None
    >>> get_version_post_release("1.2.3.post1")
    1

tools.name: get_version_dev_number
tools.description:
Get the development number of a version. version: A version string to parse and extract the development number from -> The development number of the version, or None if not a development version.
    
    >>> print(get_version_dev_number("1.2.3"))
    None
    >>> get_version_dev_number("1.2.3.dev1")
    1

tools.name: get_version_local_segment
tools.description:
Get the local version segment of a version. version: A version string to parse and extract the local version segment from
    
    >>> print(get_version_local_segment("1.2.3"))
    None
    >>> get_version_local_segment("1.2.3+abc")
    'abc'

tools.name: get_version_epoch
tools.description:
Get the epoch of a version. version: A version string to parse and extract the epoch from -> The epoch of the version.
    
    >>> get_version_epoch("2.0.0")
    0
    >>> get_version_epoch("1!2.0.0")
    1

tools.name: get_version_base
tools.description: Get the base version of a version string. version: A version string to extract the base version from e.g. '1.2.3+abc' -> '1.2.3'.

tools.name: get_version_public
tools.description: Get the public portion of a version string. version: A version string to extract the public portion from e.g. '1.2.3+abc' -> '1.2.3'.

tools.name: is_version_postrelease
tools.description: Check if a version is a post-release version. version: A version string to check if it is a post-release version -> true if post-release, false otherwise.

tools.name: is_version_devrelease
tools.description: Check if a version is a development release version. version: A version string to check if it's a development release -> true if development release, false otherwise.

tools.name: get_version_major
tools.description: Get the major version component. version: A version string to parse and extract the major version from, e.g. '1.2.3' -> 1.

tools.name: get_version_minor
tools.description:
Get the minor version component. version: A version string to parse and extract the minor version from
    
    >>> get_version_minor("1.2.3")
    2
    >>> get_version_minor("1")
    0

tools.name: get_version_micro
tools.description: Get the micro version component. version: A version string to parse, e.g. '1.2.3' -> 3.

tools.name: parse_specifier
tools.description: Parse a version specifier string into a Specifier object. specifier: A version specifier string to parse, e.g. '>=1.0.0' -> Specifier object. prereleases: Whether to allow pre-release versions.

tools.name: specifier_contains
tools.description: Check if a version is contained within a Specifier. specifier: A version specifier string, e.g., '>=1.2.3'. version: The version string to check against the specifier. prereleases: Whether or not to match prereleases with this Specifier. If set to None (the default), it will follow the recommendation from PEP 440. >>> specifier_contains('>=1.2.3', '1.2.3') True

tools.name: filter_versions_by_specifier
tools.description:
Filter items in the given iterable, that match the specifier.
    
    :param specifier: A version specifier string (e.g., '>=1.2.3')
    :param iterable: An iterable of version strings or dictionaries with version info
    :param prereleases: Whether to include prerelease versions; if None, follows PEP 440 defaults
    :return: List of items that match the specifier
    
    >>> filter_versions_by_specifier(">=1.2.3", [{"ver": "1.2"}, {"ver": "1.3"}], key=lambda x: x["ver"])
    [{'ver': '1.3'}]

tools.name: filter_versions_by_specifier_set
tools.description:
Filter an iterable of version strings to only those matching the given specifiers.
    
    Args:
        specifiers: A string representing version specifiers (e.g., '>=1.2.3')
        iterable: An iterable containing version strings or objects with version info
        prereleases: Whether to include prereleases; if None, follows PEP 440 recommendation
        
    Returns:
        A list of items that match the specifiers
        
    Example:
        >>> filter_versions_by_specifier_set(">=1.2.3", ["1.2", "1.3", "1.5a1"])
        ['1.3']

tools.name: parse_marker
tools.description: Parse a dependency marker expression into a Marker object. marker: The string representation of a marker expression, e.g. 'python_version > "3.6"' -> "<Marker('python_version > "3.6"')>".

tools.name: evaluate_marker
tools.description:
Evaluate a marker expression against an environment.
    
    Args:
        marker (str): A marker expression to evaluate
        environment (dict, optional): Mapping containing keys and values to override the detected environment
        context (str, optional): The context in which the marker is evaluated, 
                                one of "metadata", "lock_file", or "requirement"
    
    Returns:
        bool: True if the marker matches, otherwise False
    
    Example:
        >>> evaluate_marker('python_version >= "3.6"', {"python_version": "3.8"})
        True

tools.name: parse_metadata_from_email
tools.description:
Parse metadata from email headers.
    
    Args:
        data: Email headers containing distribution metadata
        validate: Whether to validate the parsed metadata
    
    Returns:
        Dictionary containing parsed metadata fields
    
    Example:
        >>> parse_metadata_from_email('Name: mypackage\nVersion: 1.0\n', True)
        {'name': 'mypackage', 'version': '1.0'}

tools.name: create_tag
tools.description: Create a Tag object representing a wheel tag triple. interpreter: The interpreter name, e.g. "py". abi: The ABI that a wheel supports, e.g. "cp37m". platform: The OS/platform the wheel supports, e.g. "win_amd64". Example: create_tag("py", "cp37m", "win_amd64") -> "py-cp37m-win_amd64".

tools.name: generate_cpython_tags
tools.description: Generate CPython interpreter tags for wheel compatibility. python_version: target Python version as [major, minor], e.g. [3, 9]. abis: compatible ABIs like ['cp39', 'abi3'], defaults to system ABIs. platforms: compatible platforms like ['linux_x86_64'], defaults to system platforms. Example: generate_cpython_tags([3, 9]) -> ['cp39-cp39-linux_x86_64', 'cp39-abi3-linux_x86_64', ...]

tools.name: generate_system_tags
tools.description: Generate tags for the running interpreter. warn: whether warnings should be logged -> list of tag strings in format 'interpreter-abi-platform'

tools.name: generate_compatible_tags
tools.description: Generate tags for an interpreter compatible with a specified Python version. python_version: A one- or two-item sequence representing the compatible version of Python, e.g. [3, 8]. interpreter: The name of the interpreter (if known), e.g. 'cp38'. -> A list of tag strings.

tools.name: generate_platform_tags
tools.description: Generate platform tags for the running interpreter. Returns a list of platform tag strings.

tools.name: get_interpreter_name
tools.description: Get the name of the running interpreter. Returns a string identifier for the current Python implementation, such as 'cp' for CPython or 'pp' for PyPy.

tools.name: get_interpreter_version
tools.description: Get the version of the running interpreter. warn: whether warnings should be logged -> e.g. '311'

tools.name: get_interpreter_abi
tools.description: Get the ABI tag of the running interpreter. Returns a string representing the ABI tag, e.g. 'cp39'.

tools.name: resolve_dependency_group
tools.description:
Resolve a dependency group to a list of requirements.
    
    :param dependency_groups: Mapping of dependency group names to their requirements
    :param group: the name of the group to resolve
    :example: resolve_dependency_group({"dev": ["pytest", "black"]}, "dev") -> ["pytest", "black"]

tools.name: lookup_dependency_group
tools.description:
Lookup a group name, returning the parsed dependency data for that group.
    This will not resolve includes.
    
    :param dependency_groups: Mapping of dependency group names to their dependencies
    :param group: the name of the group to lookup
    :example: lookup_dependency_group({"dev": ["pytest", "black"]}, "dev") -> ["pytest", "black"]
